reviews.review:
Risk of Rain is a Rougelike game from 2013 made by Hopoo games, and it might just be one of the most nostalgic yet fun games in the whole genre. Nowdays it's overshadowed by the presence of it's sequel, which is understandable, but this title should also deserve praise for how modern it was when it released, and also for how well it kept up with the times

Gameplay: 8/10

Risk of Rain pretty much defined how a Rougelike was supposed to be played, how it should be structured, how it should be balanced etc., at the time, this whole game-type barely existed, the biggest games that came close were games like The (original) Binding of Isaac, FTL: Faster Than Light and Rouge Legacy. For a game that is almost a decade old, it's suprisingly modern. The gameplay revolves around you gathering items to upgrade yourself against huge odds. These items have synergy with you and with other items, and you can get ridiculous sets and builds to suit your niche. This game is also pretty ball busting, so you need to abusive every loop-hole that you can to get a win, or to get as far as you can. Another unique mechanic to this game is the timer, that slowly builds up difficulity on your run. This timer will make you do lots of 
quick evaluations on where and how to spend your time. I could go on and on how deep this game's intricacies go. Overall solid even today.

Graphics: 8/10

Nowdays this is the thing that most people get turned off by, they think that these graphics are of a flash game or something and instantly decide that it's not worth it, but I think they're charming as all hell. The pixelart style back then wasn't as common, and even seen as weird by other game standards, but everything is well detailed, the backgrounds, the characters, the bosses everything. It reminds me of the old dos Lemmings and the 2D Worms games. It's decivingly simple yet very well thought out.

Music: 10/10

This really is the main reason I keep coming back to the game, along with the gameplay story and graphics.
I really can't describe the soundtrack of this game well enough, I'm just gonna say that it envokes nostalgia in not a crutch way, but in a really "good memory" vibe. If you, who reads this, didn't listen to the OST of this game, I recommend "Aurora Borealis", "Monsoon" and "coalescence". This soundtrack just makes me happy in a weird way.

Story: 10/10

While it's not a lot, and Im not gonna spoil it, all I can say it's a lot more dark than the story of it's sequel, and makes the graphics and the soundtrack work in conjuntion to create this atmosphere no game has. It's perfect.


Overall: 9/10

It's a forgotten classic, it has the gameplay, the music which are all knot together by the atmosphere and the story.
I would highly recommend you buying it if you like games like these. For me this game and the Original Binding of Isaac are some of my favorite video games of all time for their weirdly nostalgic atmosphere, that even I can't put my finger on, and I keep coming back from time to time to witness both of them.
